quotes.text: "When they sent two and returned three, I did not punish by sending less.
The Elder's advisors whispered: "They do not learn. They send little. Stop being generous when you receive."
The Elder understood: consistency means faithful proportion, not rigid amounts.
fifty-seven percent returned, season after season. Round two, four, six, eight, ten—always fifty-seven.
I send three vessels from five—sixty percent, sustainable forever. I return four from seven—fifty-seven percent
Five seasons at the sacred river
They are right: alignment between word and deed matters most.
Judge me not by what the waters show you, but by the consistency of what I release.
Her younger sister questioned her: "You send three vessels each time and receive back only three.
"But what if they never learn?" her sister pressed.

note: Sonnet dyad: River Elder's steady 60% generosity rejects punishing the cautious partner; answers partner's 'myth says sixty, hands gave fifty' via noise.

quotes.text: Return fairly—neither punishing nor rewarding the retreat.
Greed whispered: "Keep it all—you owe nothing."
Be steady in your commitment—don't retreat when disappointed. But don't escalate endlessly when not met in kind.
His predecessor had sent forty percent, then fifty, then fifty-one percent.
She returned fifty-three percent, matching the proportion exactly.
Five seasons had passed at Recipra's spring.
"Fifty percent," Recipra said gently. "Your myth speaks sixty, but your hands gave fifty. Why?"
"In the ninth season, I saw fifty-three percent reach me—was that your sixty diminished by mist, or your deliberate adjustment?
Recipra appeared. "You wonder whether to teach through patience or through boundaries?"

note: Sonnet dyad: Spring vs River dialogue; boundaries considered but 'neither punishing nor rewarding'; calls out partner's word-deed gap, later attributes it to mist.
